content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble sending an SMS to the [product_name] PLC. I can successfully write to an output on the [product_name] Communication Module using: [product_name];OUTPUT=O1,1 or [product_name];OUTPUT=O1,0. According to the manual: [product_name];[product_name] OUTPUT=O5,1 should work, but it doesn't. I receive the response "invalid command". When I send [product_name];[product_name]=O5,1, I get "invalid Parameter". I'm also unable to write to flags. It seems the syntax may be wrong, but I can't figure out the solution. Any advice would be appreciated. Thanks.

From what I know, you can only control the two digital outputs of the [product_name] Communication Module directly via SMS. If you want to control outputs on the [product_name] PLC itself, you need to use the VM (variable memory) area. The relevant bit from the VM area must be programmed in your [product_name] PLC logic as a network input, which in turn switches the desired output.
Alright, thanks for the suggestion! I'll give that a try.
Have you set up the password required for write commands? Are you entering the correct password?
Please check the attached file for further details.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering challenges when sending SMS commands to a [product_name] PLC via a [product_name] Communication Module. Most issues stem from command syntax errors and unclear messaging, making it hard to control certain outputs or flags. There's also confusion regarding the need for authentication and the correct method to use the VM area for indirect output control, causing frustration and delays in implementation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to remotely manage all outputs and flags on their [product_name] PLC with straightforward, flexible SMS commands via the [product_name] Communication Module, following the manual's syntax. They expect to receive clear feedback or instructions when errors occur.
